page: Microsoft Azure E64pds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Epdsv6 family, powered by a Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this server features 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs running at 3.4 GHz with a single thread per core configuration. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The processor includes 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 128 MB L3 cache, supporting cryptography acceleration via AES but lacking AVX or AMX vector extensions.

For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 3780 GB local disk and is Premium Storage capable. In benchmark evaluations, the E64pds_v6 demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, scoring in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory performance is highly efficient, with uncached large-block read and write bandwidths both ranking in the top 10%. Database operations and software compilation tasks also achieve top-tier results, while single-core performance and LLM inference speeds generally fall into the average to strong categories.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM-based architecture provides high resource density and exceptional memory bandwidth per resource unit, making it a viable alternative to traditional x86 architectures for memory-intensive workloads. The combination of 512.0 GB of RAM, 64 dedicated cores, and 3780 GB of local storage makes this server highly suitable for large-scale database deployments, memory-cached applications like Redis, software compilation pipelines, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
